question: Should OpenClaw permanently admit operator-allowlisted, already-installed `workspace-directory` Codex plugins using exact catalog IDs and app ownership/readiness checks, without installation authority?
rationale: Direct Codex source and exact-head proof validate the mechanics, but automation cannot accept a broader account-scoped plugin trust and long-term compatibility contract for maintainers.

options.title: Approve constrained workspace support
options.body: Accept exact-ID plugins only when already installed, enabled, remotely readable, and app-accessible, while preserving default-deny apps and no installation authority.

options.title: Keep curated-only support
options.body: Reject the new marketplace contract and leave workspace plugins outside native Codex turns.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained workspace support
recommendation.body: Accept exact-ID plugins only when already installed, enabled, remotely readable, and app-accessible, while preserving default-deny apps and no installation authority.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant native Codex plugin and session-policy surfaces were introduced and recently maintained by this owner.
